tasks.title: Creating a room
tasks.statement:
POST /rooms {"name":..}: the name is trimmed, its length must be 1–32 characters (otherwise 422), a repeated name is 409 (AppError::from(sqlx::Error) already translates 23505). In ONE transaction insert the room (the owner is the current user) and the member record. The response: 201, the header Location: /rooms/ID and JSON {"id":..,"name":..}. main checks success, the header, a repeat, an empty and a too long name, a missing token and the number of members.

Expected output:
«201 {"id":1,"name":"dev"}
Some("/rooms/2")
409 {"error":{"code":"conflict","message":"уже существует"}}
422
422
401
участников: 2»
tasks.hint: pool.begin(); fetch_one(&mut *tx); tx.commit(); a tuple (StatusCode, [(LOCATION, ..)], Json(..)).

GET /rooms returns a JSON array of the rooms the current user belongs to: [{"id","name","members"}] ordered by name, where members is the number of members in the room (in one query, GROUP BY). Other users' rooms are not shown. main creates the rooms by hand through SQL.

Expected output:
200 [{"id":2,"name":"dev","members":2},{"id":1,"name":"general","members":3}]
200 [{"id":1,"name":"general","members":3},{"id":3,"name":"secret","members":1}]
401

Expected output:
«204
204
204
404
строк: 1»

tasks.statement:

«204
204
409 {"error":{"code":"conflict","message":"владелец не может выйти"}}
участников: 1»

404
404

«201 {"author":"anna","id":1,"text":"привет, мир"}
404
422
201
422»

tasks.title: Validating message text
tasks.statement:
Write a pure function validate_text(raw: &str, max_chars: usize) -> Result<String, &'static str>: it removes control characters (except \n), trims whitespace at the edges, collapses three or more consecutive newlines into two, returns «пусто» if nothing is left, and «длинно» if the number of characters (chars) is greater than max_chars; otherwise Ok(trimmed text). Try it on a set of strings.

Expected output:
«"  привет  " -> Err("длинно")
"" -> Err("пусто")
"   \n  " -> Err("пусто")
"a\n\n\n\nb" -> Ok("a\n\nb")
"tab\there" -> Err("длинно")
"ёёёёё" -> Ok("ёёёёё")
"ёёёёёё" -> Err("длинно")
"  x\u{7}y  " -> Ok("xy")»

filter(|c| !c.is_control() || *c == '

tasks.title: Unread counter
tasks.statement:
GET /rooms returns a JSON array [{"id","name","unread"}] ordered by name for the current user's rooms: unread is the number of messages in the room with an id greater than their last_read, written NOT by themselves. Everything in one query (JOIN + GROUP BY + COUNT FILTER). Then POST /rooms/{id}/read {"upto":N} sets last_read = GREATEST(last_read, N) and answers 204.

Expected output:
200 [{"id":2,"name":"empty","unread":0},{"id":1,"name":"general","unread":1}]
200 [{"id":1,"name":"general","unread":5}]
204
200 [{"id":1,"name":"general","unread":1}]
204
200 [{"id":1,"name":"general","unread":1}]
tasks.hint: COUNT(msg.id) FILTER (WHERE msg.id > me.last_read AND msg.author_id <> me.user_id).

tasks.statement:
Write mark_read(&PgPool, room: i64, user: i64, upto: i64) -> i64: with one query (UPDATE ... SET last_read = GREATEST(last_read, $3) ... RETURNING last_read) it updates the marker and returns its new value. For a missing member return -1 (fetch_optional). main calls it with the sequence 5, 3, 8, 8, 2 for an existing member and once for someone who is not a member.

Expected output:
5
5
8
8
8
-1

The update sets edited_at = now(). The response is 200 and JSON {"id","text","edited":true}. Check permissions right in the UPDATE: … WHERE id = $1 AND NOT deleted AND (author_id = $2 OR room_id IN (SELECT id FROM rooms WHERE owner_id = $2)). The response is 204. Tell 403 from 404 with a second query.

«204
404
403
204
404
удалено: 2»

tasks.statement:
The history GET /rooms/{id}/messages returns the text of deleted messages. Fix the query: for rows with deleted = true the text field must return the placeholder «[сообщение удалено]», and the rows themselves stay in the output. Hint: CASE WHEN deleted THEN ... ELSE text END AS text.

tasks.title: Substring search
tasks.statement:
GET /rooms/{id}/messages/search?q=: up to 20 non-deleted messages of the room that contain q, case-insensitively, from newest to oldest ([{"id","text"}]). The characters %, _ and \ in q must be searched literally — escape them (replace) and use ILIKE ... ESCAPE '\'. An empty q is 422. A non-member gets 404.

Expected output:
«привет: 200 [{"id":4,"text":"ПРИВЕТСТВИЕ"},{"id":1,"text":"Привет, мир"}]
100%: 200 [{"id":2,"text":"скидка 100% сегодня"}]
_: 200 [{"id":3,"text":"под_черкивание"}]
%: 200 [{"id":2,"text":"скидка 100% сегодня"}]
ТЕКСТ: 200 [{"id":5,"text":"обычный текст"}]
422»
tasks.hint: let pattern = format!("%{}%", q.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('%', "\\%").replace('_', "\\_")); ... ILIKE $2 ESCAPE '\\'.

Thanks to morphology, a search for the word «собака» finds messages with the words «собака», «собаки», «собаками», but not «собрание». An empty query is 422.

tasks.title: Rate limit on posting
tasks.statement:
POST /rooms/{id}/messages {"text":..}: a user may post at most 5 messages in the last 10 seconds (count by created_at in the database: COUNT(*) WHERE author_id = $1 AND created_at > now() - interval '10 seconds'). The sixth in a row is 429 (AppError::TooMany), with the header Retry-After: 10 in the response (exactly the number of seconds in the window). A successful one is 201 and «ок». Check membership first (404 for outsiders). Test six in a row from anna and one from boris.

Expected output:
anna 1: 201
anna 2: 201
anna 3: 201
anna 4: 201
anna 5: 201
anna 6: 429
Some("10")
boris: 201
tasks.hint: Return a Response with a header: (StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, [(RETRY_AFTER, "10")], body).into_response().

tasks.title: Link to the next page
tasks.statement:
Write next_link(room: i64, items: &[i64], limit: usize, extra: &[(&str, &str)]) -> Option<String>: items are the message ids of a page from newest to oldest. If the page is not full (items.len() < limit) or empty — None. Otherwise — «/rooms/ROOM/messages?before=ID&limit=N», where ID is the last (oldest) element; the pairs from extra are appended to the end of the query as «&key=value», with values percent-encoded: a space → %20, and everything except letters, digits and «-_.~» → %XX byte by byte in UTF-8.

Expected output:
Some("/rooms/7/messages?before=28&limit=3")
None
None
Some("/rooms/1/messages?before=4&limit=2&q=hello%20world&from=%D0%BF%D1%80%D0%B8%D0%B2%D0%B5%D1%82")
Some("/rooms/1/messages?before=9&limit=1&a=x%26y%3Dz%2F~-_.")
tasks.hint: Write the function encode(&str) yourself: for b in s.bytes() ... format!("%{b:02X}").

After the transfer the former owner (if they are not the last member) can leave the room — check it with a DELETE ... members/me request (the leave handler is ready: it forbids leaving only to the owner).

tasks.title: A direct conversation as a room
tasks.statement:
Write get_or_create_dm(&PgPool, a: i64, b: i64) -> i64: a private room of two users. The name is deterministic: «dm:LOWER-HIGHER» (by id). If the room exists, its id is returned; otherwise it is created (the owner is the lower id) together with the two members in one transaction. Calling get_or_create_dm(1,2) and get_or_create_dm(2,1) must give the same room; repeated calls must not pile up rows. Solve the race of two simultaneous creators with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING and a second SELECT. Five parallel calls must give one id.

Expected output:
«1 1 true
другая пара: true
параллельно один id: true
[("dm:1-2", 1), ("dm:1-3", 1), ("dm:7-8", 7)]
участников: 6»
tasks.hint: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING; then SELECT id FROM rooms WHERE name = $1; the members — INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.

tasks.title: Message format in JSON
tasks.statement:
The struct MessageOut { id: i64, room_id: i64, author: String, text: String, created_at: DateTime<Utc>, edited_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>> } is serialized to JSON: keys in camelCase (roomId, createdAt, editedAt), edited_at is skipped when None, and the time is an RFC 3339 string in UTC. Read from the database (query_as, derive FromRow is needed; the author field comes through a JOIN with users) a message without edits and a message after UPDATE edited_at = now(), serialize them and print: the keys of each in alphabetical order, and check that createdAt parses as RFC 3339 (DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339).

Expected output:
["author", "createdAt", "id", "roomId", "text"]
true
["author", "createdAt", "editedAt", "id", "roomId", "text"]
true
tasks.hint: #[derive(Serialize, FromRow)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")].
